rationale:
SUPERSESSION RECORD (2026-10-26), measured against the analyzer's own output (script/m14/perl-fixture-divergence.mts).
CHANGED ROWS, old -> live.
  · exports alpha/beta/gamma/delta: reasonCode `exporter-surface` -> `exporter-array-declaration` (the construct is an Exporter ARRAY declaration; `exporter-surface` is kept for the %EXPORT_TAGS KEY, which is a tag name, not an exported sub) and evidenceClass `structural` -> `import_based` (the analyzer's tier pass now agrees with src/lsp/evidence_tier.ts, whose rule 2 puts the import surface at import_based).
  · imports strict/warnings/feature/Runtime::Only: reasonCode `module-load-site` -> `use-module-load`; Lazy::Load: `module-load-site` -> `runtime-require` (a `require` is a RUNTIME load and is emitted at 0.9, not 1.0 — the confidenceMax row pins that); all five evidenceClass `structural` -> `import_based`.
  · uses Config::Limits::MAX: reasonCode `qualified-name-access` -> `qualified-variable-read` (the name is a SIGIL'D package variable read; `qualified-name-access` is kept for the BAREWORD shape, which the next two rows pin).
  · references takes_code_slots beta/alpha/gamma -> `uses` with the same lines and the LEAF target: RULED 2026-10-26 that a code slot is a NAME READ AS A VALUE (`uses`), while `references` is for a name a QUERY tests. The losing label is pinned at ZERO by expectRelationshipCount.references, so a revert to `references` goes red.
  · the bareword rows `Ontology::VERSION` and `Config::Limits` are IMPLEMENTED here (they were absent before): a package-qualified bareword in value position is a read of that name.
  · the `Config::Limits::->new` row is IMPLEMENTED: the trailing-`::` leaf used to be the EMPTY string, so the edge published `.constructor` — an endpoint with no owner.
UNCHANGED: every symbol, every import/export list row, and all eight forbid rows (the hash-key control included: `Config::Only::Key` is still not a read).

Five gaps, five shapes, and each one has a near-miss that a count-only assertion could not see. (1) `exports` — the Exporter surface (`@EXPORT`, `@EXPORT_OK`, `%EXPORT_TAGS`) was payload only, so `bb_graph` could show who CONSUMES a name and never who PUBLISHES one; the names are written (L5, L7, L8, L10) and `gamma`/`delta` sit on their OWN lines inside a wrapped list, which is why the pin is a line and not the assignment's. (2) `imports` — `use strict` / `use warnings` / `use feature` (L1-3), `use Runtime::Only` (L12) and `require Lazy::Load` (L13) all load a module and produced no edge; the last is a RUNTIME load, which is why the row is `isDefault: false` in `expectImports` and a 1.0 edge in `expectRelationships`. (3) `uses` — `$Config::Limits::MAX` (L25), `Ontology::VERSION` (L26) and `Config::Limits` (L27) name another package's entity without calling it. Three near-misses are pinned as forbids because all three would have produced an edge that names no symbol at all: `Config::Limits::helper(1)` (L28) is a CALL and belongs to `calls`; `Config::Limits::MAX => 1` (L29) and `$only{Config::Only::Key}` (L31-32) are HASH KEYS. (4) `references` — `\&beta` (L37), `\&Ontology::alpha` (L38) and `\&gamma` (L40) are code-slot references, the mirror image of a call; `\&{ 'Ontology::beta' }` (L39) is a symbolic deref whose text is SOURCE CODE, and publishing it would be the same fabricated-claim defect PERL-MR12 removed from the callee side. (5) `implements` needs no row: it is emitted and pinned by `imports-and-exports`, and on this corpus it cannot fire because nothing here composes a role. (6) Two shapes the corpus census found AFTER this fixture was first written, both of which had produced an edge naming nothing: a package name spelled with a trailing `::` (`Config::Limits::->new`, L34) made the `instantiates` owner the EMPTY string and published the target `.constructor`, and `${'Ontology::hidden'}{name}` (L33) is a symbolic deref whose `varname` is a `block` node whose text carries braces and quotes. Both are pinned here because the census that found them is not a fixture and does not fail.

Measured on perl5: version::->new (cpan/version/t/02derived.t:71), IO::File::->new (dist/IO/lib/IO/Handle.pm:329), Bar::->new (dist/base/t/fields-5_6_0.t:223).

forbidRelationships.note: HASH KEY, twice: `(Config::Only::Key => 1)` on L31 and `$only{Config::Only::Key}` on L32. Both carry `::`, neither names a package entity. This row is the only thing in the fixture that can catch the position-vs-node-type defect in the guard — the first version asked whether the key was `namedChild(0)` and let both through.
`Config::Limits::helper(1)` is a CALL and already has a `calls` row; a second label on one construct is not corroboration, it is a double count
`\&Ontology::alpha` (L38) is a code-slot REFERENCE and has its own row under `references`. One label per fact is what keeps the two partitions checkable.

`\&{ 'Ontology::beta' }` (L39) is a SYMBOLIC DEREF: the grammar puts the whole expression in the slot's `function` field, so its text is source code. PERL-MR12's rule applies to a reference exactly as it does to a callee — a name has to be WRITTEN.
the same symbolic deref, read at the label it must not be published under
`package Ontology;` is a DECLARATION. A `uses`-shaped edge from the file to the class it defines would point the graph at itself, and the same reasoning retires the `uses` on a declared name.

the pre-fix shape: `leafName("Config::Limits::")` is the empty string, so the edge published an EMPTY owner. This is rule R7's fabricated endpoint in its purest form — it is the one forbid in the file that can be satisfied by a target nobody could name.

`${'Ontology::hidden'}{name}` on L33: the grammar types this `varname` as a `block` whose TEXT is `{ 'Ontology::hidden' }`, so the name carries braces and quotes. Over mojo+plack+Moose+Moo this shape produced 9 edges (moose/t/cmop/meta_package.t, moo/lib/Moo.pm:275-278) and the production noise filter deleted all 9 on its brace rule — defence in depth, but the analyzer is the thing under test, so it refuses the shape itself.
